sections.h2: Where is Alamogordo and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Alamogordo is the county seat of Otero County, in south-central New Mexico. According to Wikipedia, it sits on the eastern edge of the Tularosa Basin, against the western flank of the Sacramento Mountains, in the northernmost part of the Chihuahuan Desert. Holloman Air Force Base lies to the west.

The city was founded in June 1898 when the El Paso and Northeastern Railroad extended its line to the site, and it was incorporated in 1912. The railroad's planners laid it out with wide streets and tree-lined irrigation canals, which is why Alamogordo reads as an early planned community. White Sands National Park, created as a monument in 1933 to 1934, remains one of the main draws.

sections.h2: How much does Holloman Air Force Base matter to Alamogordo housing?
sections.html:
A great deal. Wikipedia calls Holloman the largest employer of Alamogordo residents and notes that some estimates put the base at half of the local economy. Its figures for January 2008, which are old, were 6,111 personnel directly employed and a $482 million estimated local spend.

The Air Force's own fact sheet traces the base to Alamogordo Army Air Field, renamed Holloman Air Force Base on January 13, 1948. Today MilitaryINSTALLATIONS says the 49th Wing flies the F-16 and the Reaper and supports more than 21,000 military and civilian personnel.

For a seller, this shapes demand in two ways.

  • Military families move on assignment schedules, so houses near the base often change hands because of orders and not because of a plan the owner chose.
  • Retirees stay. Wikipedia estimates about 6,700 military retirees in the area, many of whom hold a house for decades.

If you are leaving on orders with a short window, a sale that does not depend on a buyer's financing can fit a fixed report date.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Alamogordo and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Alamogordo is semi-arid, with hot summers and mild winters. Wikipedia's climate section puts typical annual rainfall at 10.63 inches, with about half arriving in the July to September monsoon.

Temperatures matter more than rain for a roof and a cooling system. The same section reports an average of 89.1 days above 90 degrees Fahrenheit, a record of 110 degrees, and 32 degrees or colder on about 55 mornings in an average winter. A coldest reading of minus 13 degrees was recorded on February 3, 2011.

In practical terms for a seller:

  • An aging evaporative or refrigerated cooling unit is a likely inspection item, because summers are long.
  • Sun damage to a flat or low-slope roof is common in dry heat, and a buyer's inspector will look at it.
  • Cold nights can freeze exposed pipes in an unoccupied house, which is worth checking if you have already moved out.

Snow is rare, with a mean of no more than 4.1 inches, so winter weather seldom delays a closing.

sections.h2: When are Otero County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Otero County lists November 10 as the date first-half tax is due, December 10 as the last day to pay it on time, April 10 for the second half, and May 10 as the last day for the second half. Those dates come from the county's own FAQ page for taxpayers.

That calendar follows the general New Mexico pattern of two installments. Interest and penalty rules are set by statute, so the county Treasurer is the right person to ask about a payoff on a specific parcel. The county also takes payment by phone or online through its Treasurer's page.

  • Alamogordo houses are valued by the Otero County Assessor, not by the city.
  • The Treasurer bills and collects for the county, the city, the school district and the state.
  • If tax is owed at sale, it is normally taken from your proceeds at closing.

Ask your closing agent for a current balance a few days before the closing date, since a due date can pass while a sale is pending.

sections.h2: What do Alamogordo sellers run into with code enforcement and old houses?
sections.html:
The city has a Code Enforcement Division, run under the Alamogordo Police Department, that works on environmental and property ordinances, and it has a page for reporting dilapidated structures. That process starts when someone emails Code Enforcement about a building.

A vacant or inherited house is the kind of property neighbors tend to report. If a notice has already arrived, it is worth resolving or disclosing it before you accept an offer.

The city's Community Development Department handles engineering and planning and zoning. Call it before any addition, garage conversion or fence, because a lender-financed buyer may ask about permits. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is does not need the work legalized first, though you should still tell them what was done.

sections.h2: What are Alamogordo's schools, college and hospital?
sections.html:
The Alamogordo Public School District serves the city, and Wikipedia lists two high schools (including Alamogordo High School), three middle schools and 11 elementary schools as of its most recent count. New Mexico State University Alamogordo, a two-year college, was founded in 1958, and the New Mexico School for the Blind and Visually Impaired dates to 1903.

Gerald Champion Regional Medical Center is a nonprofit shared military and civilian facility that also serves as the hospital for Holloman. Wikipedia reports it as the largest non-government employer in the city, with 650 employees in 2008.

These institutions give the city steady year-round employment outside the base, which is useful context when a buyer asks whether a neighborhood is stable. We do not publish school ratings, and you should confirm attendance zones with the district.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Alamogordo?
sections.html:
You can list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell for cash to a buyer who takes the house as-is. Each path has a different cost and timeline.

  • List with an agent: usually the best exposure, but you pay commission, then wait on repairs, appraisal and the buyer's loan.
  • Sell by owner: saves commission, though you handle showings, disclosures and paperwork yourself.
  • Cash sale: no lender, no appraisal contingency, and the buyer sets the closing date within reason.

Cash offers are typically below a fully repaired retail sale, and we do not quote a price without seeing the house. The trade is speed and certainty for a lower number. Alamogordo houses that tend to fit a cash sale are inherited properties, rentals with tenants, homes needing roof or cooling work, and homes owned by people with a hard move date.

Title and escrow still happen at a title company, and unpaid property tax, liens and a mortgage payoff come out of proceeds at closing.

faqs.a: Alamogordo is the county seat of Otero County in south-central New Mexico, in the Tularosa Basin at the foot of the Sacramento Mountains, with Holloman Air Force Base just to the west.

faqs.q: When are Otero County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Otero County lists November 10 for first-half tax, December 10 as the last day to pay on time, April 10 for the second half, and May 10 as the last day for it.

faqs.q: Does Holloman Air Force Base affect selling a house in Alamogordo?
faqs.a: Yes. Wikipedia calls Holloman the largest employer of Alamogordo residents, so base assignments and retirements are a steady source of both sellers and buyers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Alamogordo with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase as-is, and any open notice is paid or resolved at or before closing. Tell the buyer about it up front.

faqs.q: How hot does Alamogordo get, and does it matter for a sale?
faqs.a: Wikipedia reports about 89 days a year above 90 degrees Fahrenheit. Buyers' inspectors usually look closely at cooling equipment and roofs for that reason.

faqs.q: Who values property for tax in Alamogordo?
faqs.a: The Otero County Assessor values it and the Otero County Treasurer bills and collects the tax. The city does not run a separate property tax bill.
